name: Shore-MT
aliases: Shore Storage Manager: The Multi-Threaded Version
tagline: Multicore-scalable fork of the Shore storage manager from EPFL and CMU; a staple OLTP research testbed.
description: Shore-MT began in 2007 when Anastasia Ailamaki's DIAS lab at EPFL, with Carnegie Mellon collaborators, ported release 5.0.1 of the Shore storage manager to Pthreads and systematically removed its scalability bottlenecks: new latching and synchronisation primitives, a reworked buffer pool, lock manager and log. Their EDBT 2009 paper showed that classic engines collapsed on multicore chips while Shore-MT kept scaling. UW-Madison then completed the port and published a documented release in 2010. It provides ACID transactions with ARIES logging and recovery, B+ tree and R* tree indexes and fine-grained locking as a library, and became the base for research systems such as DORA, PLP and Shore-Kits TPC benchmarks. Development tapered off by the mid-2010s.
statusNote: Research storage manager (2007 to mid-2010s); no longer developed and its Bitbucket repository is gone. Forks continued in later research engines.
developer: EPFL DIAS lab, Carnegie Mellon University and UW-Madison

scale.notes: Scales across the cores of one SMP or NUMA machine.

strengths: Showed how to make a full ARIES-style storage manager scale on multicore CPUs
Complete transactional library: logging, recovery, locking, B+ trees and R* trees
Widely used OLTP research baseline with published TPC benchmark kits
weaknesses: No longer maintained; original code hosting has disappeared
Library only: no SQL, query processor or server
Some scalability changes were disabled as bug workarounds in the UW release
